quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 2026 (March quarter) results: CEO Stephen Chang said revenue came in slightly above the guidance midpoint, primarily reflecting strength in advanced computing (AI, servers and graphics cards), offset by softness in PC markets from seasonality and memory shortage headwinds; tablets showed strong sequential growth and Communications was better than expected on year-over-year growth from Tier 1 U.S. smartphone customers, offset by weaker demand in China. He said 'we believe the December and March quarters represent a bottom for both revenue and gross margin'. CFO Yifan Liang: DMOS revenue was $115.1 million (up 13.9% sequentially, up 7.7% year over year); Power IC revenue was $46.9 million (down 20.3% sequentially, down 14.1% year over year); assembly service and other $1.8 million (vs $2.5 million last quarter). Non-GAAP gross margin was 21.7% vs 22.2% last quarter and 22.5% a year ago, the decrease mainly from lower utilization and higher operational costs; non-GAAP operating expenses were $44.3 million (vs $41.3 million), up mainly on higher R&D; non-GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.28 (vs a loss of $0.16 last quarter). Operating cash flow was negative $8.3 million; EBITDA excluding equity method investment income and loss was $5.9 million (vs $9.7 million); cash ended at $190.3 million (vs $196.3 million); average days in inventory were 139 days (vs 140 days).

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Segment results for the March quarter (CEO Stephen Chang): Computing was up 2.1% year over year and down 0.1% sequentially at 49.1% of revenue, slightly better than guidance of a low single-digit decline, as seasonal PC declines (likely exacerbated by earlier pull-ins in calendar 2025 and rising memory pricing) were more than offset by advanced computing. Consumer was down 9.8% year over year and up 0.8% sequentially (11.8% of revenue), below expectations as a gaming recovery was offset by softness in home appliances; wearables continued strong year-over-year growth on share gains, new customer engagements and rising BOM content. Communications was up 18.7% year over year and 1.9% sequentially (20.6% of revenue), ahead of expectations for a mid-single-digit decline, driven by the Tier 1 smartphone customer and BOM content expansion, offset by softness in China. Power Supply and Industrial was 17.4% of revenue, down 13.1% year over year and up 5.3% sequentially, as quick chargers and DC fans offset sluggish solar, power tools and e-mobility. In gaming, AOS remains 'closely engaged with our leading customer on their next-generation platform', with 'a greater impact expected beginning in 2028'.
quarterly_data.figure: Computing +2.1% YoY / -0.1% QoQ, 49.1% of revenue; Consumer -9.8% YoY / +0.8% QoQ, 11.8%; Communications +18.7% YoY / +1.9% QoQ, 20.6%; Power Supply and Industrial -13.1% YoY / +5.3% QoQ, 17.4%

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Advanced computing ramp (CEO Stephen Chang): advanced computing (AI servers and graphics cards) combined more than doubled sequentially and increased more than 40% year over year, reaching 25% of the computing segment in the March quarter, which he said 'was faster than our original expectations' because of traction with medium voltage devices. Medium-voltage MOSFETs for hot swap and intermediate bus conversion 'start to take off and begin ramping in the March quarter'; AOS is shipping high-performance MOSFETs into intermediate bus converters 'now moving into the build phase at some leading ODMs for major hyperscale customers'. The solutions generally serve 48-volt to 12-volt conversion, are deployed across both GPU and CPU-based architectures, benefit from the shift toward inference workloads, and reach data center server makers, cloud service providers and hyperscalers. He said the margin on many medium voltage MOSFETs 'can actually be higher than some of our power IC products', and expects 'another quarter of strong sequential growth for advanced computing'. Graphics: a more muted environment is expected in calendar 2026 given the product cycle and allocation priorities, and graphics cards may face challenges procuring both memory and GPUs.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced computing more than doubled sequentially, up more than 40% year over year; 25% of the computing segment

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 800-volt transition view (CEO Stephen Chang): 'While we continue to view 48-volt to 12-volt intermediate bus architectures as a near-term standard that we are benefiting from today, we see this as a stepping stone towards higher voltage systems, including 800-volt architectures expected to begin emerging around 2027.'

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Medium-voltage capacity (CEO Stephen Chang, CFO Yifan Liang): 'We are actively expanding our medium voltage capacity to support this growth, and our backlog provides us with good visibility.' The expansion uses 'a mix of both internal and external' capacity: AOS is investing internally for packages done in-house while expanding other options to diversify its supply chain. March-quarter CapEx was $12.1 million vs $15 million the prior quarter; June-quarter CapEx is expected at $15 million to $17 million.
quarterly_data.figure: CapEx $12.1 million (vs $15 million prior quarter); June-quarter CapEx $15 million to $17 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: June-quarter guidance (CFO Yifan Liang): revenue approximately $168 million plus or minus $10 million; GAAP gross margin 22.3% plus or minus 1%; non-GAAP gross margin 23% plus or minus 1%; GAAP operating expenses $52 million and non-GAAP $45.5 million, each plus or minus $1 million; income tax expense $1 million to $1.2 million. The CEO said about half of the guided 130 basis point sequential gross margin improvement is expected from utilization and half from product mix. By segment (CEO): Computing up low to mid-single digits sequentially on AI and server demand; Consumer relatively flat; Communications down slightly sequentially while sustaining high year-over-year growth; Power Supply and Industrial up mid-single digits, driven by e-mobility (particularly India, with a solid backlog), DC fans tied to data center and AI infrastructure build-outs, and a modest rise in power tools. The CEO expects a return to sequential growth with margin expansion, and 'stronger growth as we exit 2026 and accelerate into 2027 and beyond', while 'calendar 2026 may reflect some near-term variability'.

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Memory shortage impact on PCs and smartphones (CEO Stephen Chang): memory supply constraints and price pressures 'represent growing headwinds for the second half of calendar 2026'. In PCs, some customers are building out sooner to get products out, and there is 'a lot of uncertainty about the second half'; AOS expects some decline in the PC market in calendar 2026 but believes it should outpace the market on BOM content from its total solutions on next-generation platforms such as Intel's Panther Lake. In smartphones, AOS is prioritizing capacity for its Tier 1 U.S. smartphone customers and premium models, which it expects to be more resilient to memory shortages, and increasing charging currents let it introduce new higher-ASP products; it still expects continued smartphone growth in calendar 2026. Tablets were expected to decline in the June quarter mostly on seasonality and increased capacity allocation to smartphone opportunities.

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and input costs: CEO Stephen Chang said 'In the March quarter, we saw a slower ASP erosion than in the December quarter. It looks like the pricing environment is improving', though AOS counts more on product mix and new products for margin improvement. CFO Yifan Liang: 'We are seeing some increases in input costs', including some material costs and some foundry subcontractors' prices; these and the pricing environment 'are already reflected in our guidance for the June quarter'.
